newsitem.title: INDIA: India Bank of Baroda cuts prime rate to 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: India Bank of Baroda cuts prime rate to 15 pct.

text.p: India's Bank of Baroda on Saturday announced a 0.5 percentage point cut in its prime lending rate to 15.0 percent, becoming the first bank to act in the wake of a series of central bank measures to relax credit policy.
The Bank of Baroda rate had one of the lowest prime rates among Indian banks before its move. Other banks prime rates range up to 19.0 percent.

Reserve Bank of India governor Chakravarty Rangarajan had earlier said he expected banks to cut their prime rates by at least one percentage point immediately following the the central bank's measures to increease liquidity in the banking system.
Rangarajan was addressing a press conference outlining RBI monetary policy for the final six months of 1996/97 (April-March).
The Bank of Baroda cut, announced by its chairman K. Kannan, will come into effect on October 21. The bank's deposit rates would also be revised downwards.

"The RBI has reduced the cap on interest rates from 11 percent to 10 percent. Accordingly we will reduce deposit interest by one percentage point for all the four slabs below one year," he told Reuters.
The bank will offer 11 percent interest on deposits with a maturity of above one year and up to two years.
